# sv0c/sv0vm: backend-enforced non-eliding explicit write

## purpose

Unblocks `sv0-strings` **SS-201** (`Track L — Future`, BL-101): a backend-enforced
guarantee that a write to a buffer survives dead-store elimination even when the
buffer is otherwise dead after the call — the missing piece behind
`strings_bytes::fill_explicit` / `strings_c23::memset_explicit`, which have stayed
`Blocked` (unexported, not aliased to plain `fill`) since SS-108/SS-148 rather than
ship an unenforced guarantee. This is **SS-U11** in `sv0-strings`'s own Track U
table (`task/sv0-strings-checklist.Rmd:114`), promoted here to its own doc because
it is a genuine sv0c/sv0vm **language/backend** feature, not a library-side slice —
any future sv0 package wanting a scrubbing primitive (crypto key material, M5's own
`crypto::*` tier) needs the same guarantee.

**Non-goals**: this is not a general `volatile` type qualifier, not a memory model
change, and not related to `unsafe`/raw pointers (see the separate
`task/sv0c-ffi-raw-pointer-abi.Rmd` for that). It is one narrowly-scoped intrinsic:
"zero (or fill) this byte range, and the backend MUST NOT optimize the write away."

## grounding audit (2026-09-14)

**Why the gap is real, not just undocumented**: `sv0-strings/docs/fill-explicit-blocked.md`
already did the negative-evidence work at SS-108 —

- **C backend**: a fill lowers to bare element stores (`codegen.sv0`'s normal
  slice-index-assignment path) with no `volatile` qualifier, no compiler barrier,
  and no `explicit_bzero`/`memset_s` call. `-O2` dead-store elimination MAY drop
  the entire loop if the buffer is provably dead after the call — this is
  precisely the vulnerability class C23 added `memset_explicit` to close, and sv0c
  has no equivalent.
- **VM backend**: sv0vm executes every `idx_set`/store opcode today (there is no
  dead-code-elimination pass over bytecode), so nothing currently drops the write
  — but there is no dedicated opcode or documented guarantee that a *future*
  bytecode optimizer (were one added) could not legally elide it. "Happens to
  retain" is not "backend-enforced."

**Existing infrastructure to reuse, not rebuild** (same shape as SS-U16's
`string_from_bytes`/`string_byte_view`): both backends already have a working
name-based intrinsic pipeline —

- `sv0c/lib/resolver.sv0`: `is_intrinsic`, `intrinsic_arity`, per-name arity/type
  tables (`string_concat` etc. as the template).
- `sv0c/lib/checker.sv0`: `BUILTIN_COUNT`, a builtin-ID dispatch resolved
  alongside ordinary `fn_table` calls (`resolve_call_or_builtin`).
- Per-backend lowering: `codegen.sv0` (C emission) and `vm_codegen.sv0` (bytecode
  emission) each already special-case every existing intrinsic by builtin ID.
- `sv0vm`'s interpreter (`sv0vm/src/interpreter/interpreter.sml`) already has a
  `CALL_BUILTIN` dispatch (SS-U16 added builtin ids 35/36 there) — a new builtin
  id is a small, well-trodden addition, not a new opcode class.

So the real work is **not** inventing new AST/parser/VM machinery — it is (a)
deciding the C-side lowering strategy, (b) adding one new builtin id end-to-end
through the existing pipeline on both backends, and (c) the sv0doc side-effect
rule making the guarantee normative, not just an implementation detail.

## scope decisions (draft — confirm before slicing)

1. **C-side lowering strategy.** Two real options, not mutually exclusive:
   - **(a) Compiler barrier via `volatile`**: emit the fill loop through a
     `volatile unsigned char *` pointer. Portable (ISO C), no platform
     dependency, but slightly weaker than a real barrier on some optimizing
     linkers (LTO across translation units is the known edge case — not a
     concern for sv0c's own single-TU-per-build C emission today).
   - **(b) Shell to the platform's real primitive when available**: detect
     `explicit_bzero` (BSD/glibc ≥ 2.25) or `memset_s` (C11 Annex K, rare) at
     `cc` capability-probe time (the same probe pattern `native_exe_cc_probe`
     already uses for other capabilities) and call it directly when present,
     falling back to (a) otherwise.
   - **Recommendation**: ship (a) unconditionally first (it needs no probe, no
     platform branching, and is sufficient for the guarantee SS-108 actually
     asks for); land (b) as a strictly-better follow-up once (a) is proven, not
     a blocking prerequisite.
2. **VM-side guarantee.** Add a dedicated opcode (not just a `CALL_BUILTIN` id)
   whose semantics are pinned in `sv0vm`'s own opcode contract as "never
   eligible for dead-store elimination by any future optimizer pass" — cheaper
   to reserve the opcode number now (bytecode format is versioned) than to
   retrofit the guarantee onto an existing generic store opcode later.
3. **Surface**: one new intrinsic, tentatively `__sv0_fill_explicit(dst: &mut
   [byte], value: byte) -> ()` at the language level (double-underscore /
   compiler-recognized, matching how other cross-cutting intrinsics are named),
   with `strings_bytes::fill_explicit` becoming a thin wrapper once it lands —
   confirm naming against sv0doc §7 conventions before implementation.

## epics

**Epic A — sv0doc normative rule.** Document the guarantee itself (what "backend
non-eliding" means precisely, and what it does NOT promise — e.g., not a real
timing-side-channel guarantee, not `volatile`'s full C semantics) in
`sv0doc/memory-model/` or `sv0doc/type-system/` (confirm placement — this is
UP-014's own §7.1 area). This is the artifact SS-U11's own row already names
("sv0doc side-effect rule").

**Epic B — C backend lowering.** The `volatile`-pointer fill loop (scope decision
1a); a differential/regression fixture proving `-O2 -DDCE_STRESS` (or equivalent)
does not eliminate a store to an otherwise-dead buffer — this needs a *real*,
externally-observable check (e.g. write to a heap buffer, `free` it, and diff
against a reference build compiled with the naive lowering to prove the naive one
elides and the new one doesn't), not just "the C compiles."

**Epic C — VM backend lowering.** The new dedicated non-elidable-store opcode;
`sv0vm` interpreter support; the opcode's contract pinned in
`sv0vm/doc/bytecode-format.md` (or wherever the opcode table is documented today
— confirm path) as never-eligible-for-elision, so a future VM optimizer pass has
an unambiguous constraint to respect.

**Epic D — end-to-end intrinsic wiring.** Resolver/checker/both-codegen
plumbing for the new builtin id (mechanical, following the SS-U16 pattern
exactly); cross-backend behavioral test (`test/vm-parity/` style) proving C and
VM agree on ordinary (non-DCE-stress) fill behavior, since the parity gate this
whole toolchain already runs would catch any accidental divergence.

**Epic E — sv0-strings consumer slice (SS-201, in sv0-strings).** Once Epics
A–D land and are pinned upstream, `strings_bytes::fill_explicit` /
`strings_c23::memset_explicit` become real exported functions wrapping the new
intrinsic; the existing `test/compile_fail/fill_explicit_blocked.sv0` /
`c23_memset_explicit_blocked.sv0` probes flip from "symbol must not resolve" to
deleted (superseded by real positive fixtures), and `docs/fill-explicit-blocked.md`
gets its "unblocked" update. This is `sv0-strings`-side work, tracked as SS-201
in its own checklist, not part of this doc's slice table.

## sliced backlog (draft — `NEW-###`)

| id | epic | slice | depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| NEW-001 | A | sv0doc: write the non-eliding-write normative rule (what's guaranteed, what isn't) | — |
| NEW-002 | B | C backend: `volatile`-pointer lowering for the new intrinsic | NEW-001 |
| NEW-003 | B | DCE-stress regression fixture proving the naive lowering elides and the new one doesn't | NEW-002 |
| NEW-004 | C | Reserve + document the new VM opcode's non-elision contract | NEW-001 |
| NEW-005 | C | `sv0vm` interpreter: implement the opcode | NEW-004 |
| NEW-006 | D | Resolver/checker: new builtin id, arity, name table entries | NEW-002, NEW-005 |
| NEW-007 | D | Both-backend codegen wiring (`codegen.sv0` builtin-id case, `vm_codegen.sv0` opcode emission) | NEW-006 |

Sequencing: A is a pure-doc slice and can start immediately in parallel with
nothing; B and C are independent of each other and can run in parallel once A
lands; D needs both B and C done; E (in `sv0-strings`) needs D done and pinned.

## completion criteria

- [ ] Epic A doc merged, cited by name from `sv0-strings/docs/fill-explicit-blocked.md`.
- [ ] NEW-003's DCE-stress fixture is red on the naive lowering and green on the
      new one — proof the guarantee is real, not just "it compiles."
- [ ] NEW-008 cross-backend parity fixture green in CI on both `sv0c` and
      `sv0vm`.
- [ ] `sv0-strings` SS-201 lands, `fill_explicit`/`memset_explicit` ship as real
      exported functions, and the two `compile_fail` "stays blocked" probes are
      retired.

## open questions

- Exact intrinsic name and whether it should be a single `fill_explicit(dst,
  value)` or a more general "mark this write non-elidable" primitive other
  future code (e.g. M5 crypto key zeroing) could reuse directly rather than
  going through `strings_bytes`.
- Where the VM opcode table is authoritatively documented today (confirm path
  before Epic C starts) — reserve the next free opcode number there, not an
  ad-hoc one.
- Whether Epic B's `volatile` lowering needs an explicit compiler-barrier
  intrinsic (e.g. an inline-asm empty clobber) in addition to `volatile`, for
  compilers where `volatile` alone has been shown insufficient across
  translation-unit boundaries (LTO) — likely out of scope for sv0c's current
  single-TU C emission model, but worth a one-line rationale note either way.
